transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2027-05-27 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (CTO - Silverpine Labs), Priya Sharma (ML Engineer), Aaron Blake (SRE), Maya Li (Product)

Summary:
Quick lab inspection of sprint-6 bench results, discuss routing/fallback decision and whether to request dedicated slot for final pilot. Compare Redwood's latency/throughput vs their incumbent baseline. Agreed to run extended throughput run and exchange SOC2 docs; possible one-week pilot extension.

Topics:
- Sprint 6 bench numbers (p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained RPS)
- Routing decision: primary hosted with dedicated fallback vs full dedicated pool
- Quantization/batching tradeoffs and KV cache behavior
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS) and legal next steps
- Acceptance criteria for pilot success

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood AE): ok thanks everyone for hopping on. quick agenda — we looked at sprint six, we wanted to walk through the lab inspection numbers and then decide routing playbook. lena you got the slide with the p95s?
[00:24] Lena (Redwood SE): yeah opening it now. quick note — these are the lab numbers from the dedicated-like environment using q4_0 quant, batch 8 for chat completions, kv cache enabled, and some prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[00:39] Tom (Silverpine CTO): sorry can you repeat q4_0? we mostly tested the incumbent with int8 earlier, want to make sure apples to apples.
[00:47] Lena (Redwood SE): right q4_0 is approximate 4-bit quant. we did a parity run with the incumbent's int8 small model. results — Redwood median (p50) latency 62ms, p95 120ms, p99 210ms for 512-token average. incumbent p50 210ms, p95 420ms, p99 610ms for same request mix. throughput sustained 110 rps on our config vs incumbent ~28 rps.
[01:18] Priya (ML Engineer): wow that delta on throughput is — that seems... is that including cold starts and kv warmup or fully steady-state?
[01:26] Lena: steady-state after warmup. first 30 seconds you see a warmup spike, but these numbers exclude the warmup window. also batch sizes and continuous batching are tuned; when we forced smaller max batch the p95 got a bit better but throughput drops.
[01:40] Aaron (SRE): what about memory pressure — we saw some occassional 504s in the 1am run. was that a routing issue or OOM?
[01:48] Lena: those 504s were from the test harness hitting a single GPU with concurrent KV heavy requests. KV cache eviction threshold was hit — K V cash, uh sorry — kv cache. we tuned eviction and it went away. recommended routing is to route short responses to hosted, longer context to dedicated slots.
[02:05] Maya (Product): do we need dedicated right away? cost is a real concern — the CFO pushed back on reserved capacity pricing.
[02:12] Evan: totally — that's why we presented two options: 1) Hosted primary with a reserved dedicated pool only for long-context or high-throughput endpoints, or 2) Full dedicated for everything. Option 1 gives lowest baseline cost and still meets latency SLOs.
[02:26] Tom: what are the unit cost deltas? we need to make sure this isn't cheaper latency but massively more expensive per token.
[02:33] Evan: we estimated unit compute cost: Redwood run in this config about $0.0032 per 1k tokens at current reserved-rate assumptions; incumbent was approx $0.0048 per 1k tokens at their published numbers, but your real spend with them considering retries was closer to $0.006. so even with dedicated reserved slot amortization it's still in the same ballpark or better for you given throughput efficiencies.
[02:58] Priya: those numbers assumed batch 8 — if we drop batch to prioritize p50/p95 we lose some efficiency. how sensitive is p95 to batch size?
[03:06] Lena: p95 is mildly sensitive. batch 8 -> p95 120ms. batch 4 -> p95 ~160ms, throughput drops ~30%. it's a tradeoff.
[03:18] Tom: security question — KMS integration? we have to use our HSM and audit logs, SOC2 compliance.
[03:25] Evan: yes we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations for Private deployments. for Hosted we encrypt at rest with KMS and provide audit logs. we'll share SOC2 summary and a SOC2 letter for your security team.
[03:36] Aaron: also need SSO/SAML and RBAC for team access — we can't have broad keys in the wild.
[03:41] Lena: SSO + SCIM + RBAC supported in the console. for pilot we can do per-token scoped creds and short TTLs.
[03:47] Tom: how about fallback behavior — if dedicated pool saturates what happens? do requests fail or fallback to smaller model?
[03:53] Lena: we have routing policies. priority flow: try dedicated slot -> if capacity saturated, fallback to hosted compatible model (smaller variant) with graceful degradation. you can configure per-route fallbacks, and we can set a hard throttle as last resort so requests queue or degrade based on business logic.
[04:10] Priya: curious about hallucination/regression risk when switching to a smaller variant — do we measure quality delta?
[04:16] Evan: yes we include eval hooks per rollout. can run canary on 1% traffic and monitor quality metrics like F1 on your evals before full switch.
[04:25] Tom: ok about the extended throughput run. lena you can outline what you'll execute?
[04:29] Lena: plan is 2 hours sustained at target request mix: 60% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 30% mid (129-512), 10% long (>512) average token ~310. target sustained RPS 120, with 10k burst. we'll collect p50/p95/p99, error rates, CPU/GPU per-slot utilization, kv hit rate, and queue latency. will share logs and JMX metrics.
[04:54] Aaron: will that require dedicated slots for the run? we don't want noisy neighbor effects.
[04:59] Lena: we'll run in a reserved test pool to isolate. that is the dedicated-like environment.
[05:03] Tom: timeline — when can we see that?
[05:06] Lena: we can schedule the extended run Thursday 2027-06-03 and deliver results by EOD same day.
[05:12] Evan: and we'll send SOC2 and the dedicated slot pricing breakdown by Tuesday 2027-06-01
[05:18] Maya: and if those numbers look good we potentially extend the pilot one week to include production key rotation and canary traffic.
[05:24] Priya: got it. small note — during the last run we saw degraded perf when we hit the KV eviction threshold. is there a way to pre-warm or pin common prefixes?
[05:33] Lena: yes we can pre-populate the KV cache for key prefixes and pin hot keys. also we can set a sticky routing so specific customers' queries hit same slot for warming.
[05:44] Tom: competitor question — we benchmarked IncumbentAI at the start. can you include the raw benchmark traces vs IncumbentAI and CloudVendorX for our SRE to review?
[05:53] Evan: yes we'll include raw traces and the JMeter harness config. note IncumbentAI had higher retry rate which pushed effective latency higher; raw p95 numbers are in the report.
[06:03] Aaron: about SLA — do you have standard uptime SLA for Dedicated? we need 99.9 minimum.
[06:09] Evan: Dedicated has SLA options up to 99.95 with enterprise package; we'll include proposed SLA language for pilot in the doc.
[06:15] Priya: testing note — please include model temperature and top_p in the run artifacts; our prompts are temperature 0.2 and that affects token generation time.
[06:23] Lena: noted. we'll capture model config and reproducible seeds, also include the prompt bank we used for the run.
[06:30] Tom: ok let's recap final deliverables.
[06:33] Evan: recap — Redwood will: 1) send SOC2 summary and dedicated pricing (Evan) 2) run extended throughput test and share logs (Lena) 3) share raw benchmark traces vs incumbents and harness config (Evan) 4) draft pilot extension terms and SLA proposal for your legal (Evan).
[06:53] Tom: and we'll confirm budget and acceptance criteria, and let you know if we want the one-week extension. thanks all — any last questions?
[07:01] Priya: nothing from me. Aaron: fine. Maya: can you include a short checklist for production rollout? that'll help our product team.
[07:08] Evan: yes we'll add a 7-item checklist: config, secrets, SSO, canary route, monitoring hooks, eviction thresholds, rollback plan.
[07:17] Tom: great. we'll wait for the SOC2 and the throughput run. talk soon.
[07:22] Evan: thanks everyone, end.
